title.target: Advanced phrasal verbs 2: feelings and relationships
title.en: Advanced phrasal verbs 2: feelings and relationships

ex.t: I get on with my new colleagues.
I don't want to let him down.
I came across an old photo.
I can't put up with it any more.

title.ko: get on with · fall out · look up to · cheer up · let down · come across
title.en: get on with · fall out · look up to · cheer up · let down · come across

explain.ko: 사람과의 관계, 감정을 나타내는 구동사는 일상 대화에서 매우 자주 쓰입니다. 관계: get on with(잘 지내다), fall out with(다투다), make up(화해하다), look up to(존경하다), put up with(참다). 감정: cheer up(기운 내다/내게 하다), let down(실망시키다), get over(극복하다), count on(믿다), come across(우연히 발견하다). 목적어가 대명사이면 분리형은 사이에 둡니다(cheer me up). 전치사가 두 개인 구동사(look up to, put up with)는 분리되지 않으므로 목적어는 맨 끝에 옵니다.
explain.en: Phrasal verbs for feelings and relationships are very common in everyday talk. Relationships: get on with, fall out with, make up, look up to, put up with. Feelings: cheer up, let down, get over, count on, come across. When the object is a pronoun, separable verbs take it in the middle (cheer me up). Three-part phrasal verbs (look up to, put up with) are inseparable, so the object comes last.

head: 구동사 / Phrasal verb
의미 / Meaning
예문 / Example
rows: I get on with my boss.
She fell out with her sister.

notes.ko: 분리형은 대명사 목적어를 사이에 둡니다. let me down(○)
notes.en: Separable verbs take a pronoun in the middle: let me down.

notes.ko: 3단어 구동사는 목적어가 끝에 옵니다. look up to him(○)
notes.en: Three-part verbs keep the object at the end: look up to him.

notes.ko: 구동사는 일상체이므로 공식 글에서는 한 단어로 바꾸는 것이 좋습니다.
notes.en: Phrasal verbs are informal; use one-word verbs in formal writing.

lines.t: Why did you fall out with your friend?
Do you get on with your new colleagues?

Yes. A friend who cheers you up when you're down is precious.

lines.t: I have looked up to my brother since I was a child. We sometimes fall out but soon make up. Whenever I was down, he cheered me up. I never want to let him down.

trans.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 형을 존경해 왔습니다. 우리는 가끔 다투지만 곧 화해합니다. 형은 제가 힘들 때마다 기운 나게 해 주었습니다. 저는 그를 절대 실망시키고 싶지 않습니다.

questions.q: Who does the speaker look up to?

lines.t: I fell out with a colleague and it's hard.
The way we work. I can't put up with it any more.

trans.ko:

items.passage:
BLOG
Recently I came across an old photo album. It reminded me of falling out and making up with friends at school. We've lost touch now, but they were people I could count on whenever I was down. So I decided to get in touch with them.

prompt.ko: 관계와 감정에 관한 구동사 4개를 써서 친구나 가족에 대해 4문장으로 써 보세요.
prompt.en: Write 4 sentences about a friend or family member, using four phrasal verbs about feelings and relationships.

task.model: I get on well with my new colleagues. I fell out with a friend last month, but we soon made up. When a friend is sad, I want to cheer them up. I want to be someone they can always count on.

model_trans.ko: 저는 새 동료들과 잘 지내고 있어요. 지난달에 친구와 다퉜지만 곧 화해했어요. 친구가 힘들 때는 제가 기운 나게 해 주고 싶어요. 저는 언제나 믿을 수 있는 사람이 되고 싶어요.
model_trans.en: I get on well with my new colleagues. I fell out with a friend last month, but we soon made up. When a friend is sad, I want to cheer them up. I want to be someone they can always count on.
